input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: The guard uses all(...) instead of any(...) over the arguments' help attributes, so the section is gated on every argument being documented rather than on at least one.
- failure path: A command with arguments SRC (help set) and DST (no help) prints no 'Positional arguments' section at all in --help, silently dropping the documented text; conversely a command with zero arguments satisfies all([]) and prints an empty 'Positional arguments' header on every --help.

Reviewer finding
- description: The condition uses all(...) where the docstring says "if at least one is documented"; it should be any(...). The section now shows only when every argument has help.
- rationale: Trigger: a command with two arguments where only one has help. all() returns False, so the whole Positional arguments section is omitted and the documented argument disappears from the help output. Conversely, a command with no arguments makes all([]) True, so an empty "Positional arguments" section header is emitted with no entries.
critique: The finding names the same faulty operation: all() is used where any() is needed to gate the Positional arguments section. It describes both consequences from the label: the section is dropped when only some arguments are documented, and an empty header is printed when there are no arguments because all([]) is True.
